- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) and price is near recent mean, model often fails to mean-revert; apply a 3–5 day moving average correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to over-predict in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is low and price is near historical low, model often underestimates recovery; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.15 and price <60.00.
